stage1.impression: A moody, believable storm plate: a lone amber speaker standing in a rain-pocked channel of water on a dark plain, a bright band low under a heavy deck, and the horn reading well against it. But the light is a warm beige overcast, not acid; the speaker is lit flat from the front with no rim from the sun behind it; the ground reads as a choppy sea more than as wet lava; and the glassy splash crowns and the post-like rain streaks over the far field say render.

blocking_9: The world reads sulphurous yellow-green: the sky and haze lean green, not beige (upper sky b_median well under r and g, g >= r)
The light visibly comes from behind: a bright rim on the speaker's right edge and on the horn, and backlit rain streaks glowing on the sun side
The ground reads at once as wet volcanic rock at real scale (large pillows, boulders, breaks in the pattern), not a uniform chop that looks like the sea
No seam between the modelled ground and the far field or horizon
Splashes read as water hitting water (ripple rings, small spray), not glassy tulip-shaped crowns
Rain streaks near the ground fade out instead of standing as short bright sticks above the far field
The speaker's edges are crisp where focus falls (edge 10-90 width of a few px at proof size, not 17-22)

defects.what: Sky and horizon band are warm neutral beige (sky r163 g160 b132; band r207 g199 b165), not the sulphurous yellow-green the frame is for
No rim on the right edge toward the sun: the right face (lum 106) is darker than the left (127); the backlight never reaches the product
Ground is a uniform, same-scale chop of displaced bumps; reads as dark choppy sea, not rock; no boulders read in the mid-ground
A lighter strip and a step where the near ground meets the far field, a visible seam under the horizon
Splash crowns are glassy, identical tulip shapes, evenly scattered across the puddle; read as CG instances
Rain streaks over the far field stop short above the ground and read as short bright vertical sticks or posts
A soft out-of-focus vertical smear at the left edge (near drop layer) reads as a lens artefact
Product edges are soft at proof size (edge 10-90 width 17-22 px at the cabinet sides)
Overall low contrast and haze over everything; no true blacks (p1 26) so the image feels greyed rather than stormy

changes.problem: The world is beige overcast, not acid: nothing in the sky or air is yellow-green.

evidence.measured: upper sky r163 g160 b132; horizon band [0,300,500,400] r207 g199 b165; ground near-neutral r50 g52 b43

change.setting: Haze colour and density; sky (HDRI) tint
change.to: haze #B7BC5E at 0.0028 /m; multiply the HDRI by #E6E8A0 (keep its strength 0.13); leave white balance and tint as they are so the speaker's colour holds

changes.expected: The sky and horizon band go sulphur-green (g at or above r, blue clearly down); the far field takes the same cast; the speaker stays golden amber.

changes.problem: The sun is behind the speaker but it is lit from the front: no rim, the right face is the darker one.

evidence.measured: right edge strip lum_median 90; right face [640,420,690,550] lum 106 vs left face 127

change.setting: Rim card behind right (toward the sun); front reflector
change.from: rim card 1.5 m at 9.0; reflector 2 m at 4.0
change.to: rim card 1.0 m at 22.0, moved 30 cm closer to the cabinet's right rear edge and raised to cover the horn as well; reflector 2.5

changes.expected: A bright, narrow line of light down the cabinet's right edge and along the horn's right lip; the front falls slightly darker, so the light reads as coming from behind.

changes.problem: The light does not break through behind the rain: the rain does not catch the sun, and the sun side of the sky is only a little brighter.

evidence.measured: right sky lum_median 214 vs left [0,200,300,420] 186; streaks the same brightness across the frame

change.setting: Sky rotation (sun azimuth with the sun lamp); rain forward scattering
change.from: sun 20 deg right of the camera's axis; streak scattering as is
change.to: rotate the HDRI and the sun lamp together so the sun is 14 deg right (still just out of frame); raise the streaks' forward-scattering anisotropy to 0.8

changes.expected: The right third of the sky warms and brightens toward the sun, and the streaks on the right half glow against the darker cloud.

changes.problem: The ground reads as a choppy sea: one scale of bump everywhere, no rock forms or boulders read.

evidence.measured: lum_range 35 (p5 35, p95 70); same chop pattern left and right; boulders not visible in the mid-ground

change.from: true displacement 7 cm of one dominant chop scale; boulders mostly hidden
change.to: cut the 20 to 60 cm grain to half amplitude; raise the pillow forms (1.5 to 4 m) to 25 cm; place two wet scanned boulders at 5 to 8 m either side of the speaker, one breaking the left mid-ground, one smaller at right; put dry, rougher tops (film roughness 0.35) on the high points

changes.expected: The mid-ground breaks into large rounded pillows with darker gaps and a couple of boulders; the sea-like chop goes; contrast rises in the mid-ground.

changes.problem: The splash crowns are glassy, identical and evenly spread; they read as CG instances.

evidence.measured: visible repeated tulip-shaped crowns across the puddle in the crop; same size and opacity

change.from: 700 crowns 2 to 20 mm within 3 m (opacity 0.15); 900 at 3 to 10 m
change.to: 250 crowns 2 to 8 mm within 3 m (opacity 0.08), each with a secondary droplet ring and a short-lived ripple; 400 at 3 to 10 m; double the smallest ripple ring layer

changes.expected: The puddle reads as rain hitting water: rings and pinprick spray, no tulip shapes.

changes.problem: A light strip and step under the horizon shows where the near ground meets the far field.

evidence.measured: a lighter band (lum about 100 to 190) sits between the far ridge and the dark near field; visible hard step at about y 450 in the left crop; strip [0,425,500,450] lum_median 114

change.from: far field 3 m a tile, film roughness 0.18, flat to the horizon; haze box to 900 m
change.to: blend the near and far ground over 20 to 60 m with a noise mask; raise the far field's film roughness to 0.3 so it stops mirroring the bright band; add a low ground-hugging haze layer 0 to 3 m high at 0.006 /m from 40 m out

changes.expected: The ground darkens and fades evenly into haze with no strip or step under the horizon.

changes.problem: Streaks over the far field end in mid-air as short bright sticks.

evidence.measured: several isolated vertical bright marks 30 to 40 px long standing above the ground at x about 140, 280, 430

change.from: opacity 0.12 to 0.5, none ending within 30 cm of the ground
change.to: opacity cap 0.3 below the horizon line, fade the last 40 % of each streak, and let streaks end on the ground (drop the 30 cm rule)

changes.expected: Rain over the far field reads as a fine, even veil, no individual posts.

changes.problem: Edges are soft and the image is greyed: no true blacks and soft cabinet edges.

evidence.measured: edge step -40 over 17 px (right), -45 over 22 px (left); whole-frame p1 26; foreground rock [0,650,300,800] p5 20.7

change.to: contrast 0.22, clarity 0.10, sharpen 0.45, with a black point lift removed so p1 sits near 12

changes.expected: Deeper shadows in the rock and the woofer, crisper cabinet edges.

out_of_scope.request: Make the white lining read less like opaque cream card through the acrylic
out_of_scope.why: It is the speaker's material and colour, which are fixed; the internal boards read flat and cardboard-like at this size.
